Still, these things, when developed and cultivated, lead to blissful meditation in this life, and also to mindfulness and situational awareness.”

22.124.s: Atha kho āyasmā kappo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā kappo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
22.124.e: Then Venerable Kappa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

22.124.s: “kathaṁ nu kho, bhante, jānato kathaṁ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā na hontī”ti?
22.124.e: “Sir, how does one know and see so that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs?”

22.124.s: “Yaṁ kiñci, kappa, rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
22.124.e: “Kappa, one truly sees any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

22.124.s: Yā kāci vedanā …pe… yā kāci saññā … ye keci saṅkhārā … yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
22.124.e: One truly sees any kind of feeling … perception … choices … consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

22.124.s: Evaṁ kho, kappa, jānato evaṁ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā na hontī”ti.
22.124.e: That’s how to know and see so that there’s no I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs.”

22.125.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā kappo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
22.125.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Kappa said to the Buddha:

22.125.s: “kathaṁ nu kho, bhante, jānato kathaṁ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṁ mānasaṁ hoti vidhā samatikkantaṁ santaṁ suvimuttan”ti?
22.125.e: “Sir, how does one know and see so that the heart is rid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs; and going beyond discrimination, it’s peaceful and well freed?”

22.125.s: “Yaṁ kiñci, kappa, rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ …pe… sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā anupādāvimutto hoti.
22.125.e: “Kappa, one is freed by not grasping having truly seen any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

22.125.s: Yā kāci vedanā … yā kāci saññā … ye keci saṅkhārā … yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā anupādāvimutto hoti.
22.125.e: One is freed by not grasping having truly seen any kind of feeling … perception … choices … consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

22.125.s: Evaṁ kho, kappa, jānato evaṁ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānāpagataṁ mānasaṁ hoti vidhā samatikkantaṁ santaṁ suvimuttan”ti.
22.125.e: That’s how to know and see so that the heart is rid of I-making, mine-making, and conceit for this conscious body and externally for all signs; and going beyond discrimination, it’s peaceful and well freed.”

22.126.s: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
22.126.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

22.126.s: “‘avijjā, avijjā’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, avijjā; kittāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti?
22.126.e: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’. What is ignorance? And how is an ignoramus defined?”

22.126.s: “Idha, bhikkhu, assutavā puthujjano samudayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; vayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘vayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
22.126.e: “Mendicant, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t truly understand form, which is liable to originate, as form which is liable to originate. They don’t truly understand form, which is liable to vanish, as form which is liable to vanish. They don’t truly understand form, which is liable to originate and vanish, as form which is liable to originate and vanish.

22.126.s: Samudayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘samudayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; vayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘vayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti. Samudayadhammaṁ saññaṁ …pe… samudayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘samudayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; vayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘vayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; samudayavayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘samudayavayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti. Samudayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; vayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘vayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
22.126.e: They don’t truly understand feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, which is liable to originate, as consciousness which is liable to originate. They don’t truly understand consciousness, which is liable to vanish, as consciousness which is liable to vanish. They don’t truly understand consciousness, which is liable to originate and vanish, as consciousness which is liable to originate and vanish.

22.126.s: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu, avijjā; ettāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.126.e: This is called ignorance. And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

22.126.s: Evaṁ vutte, so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
22.126.e: When he said this, the mendicant said to the Buddha:

22.126.s: “‘vijjā, vijjā’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, vijjā; kittāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti?
22.126.e: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘knowledge’. What is knowledge? And how is a knowing one defined?”

22.126.s: “Idha, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako samudayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; vayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘vayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
22.126.e: “Mendicant, it’s when a learned noble disciple truly understands form, which is liable to originate, as form which is liable to originate. They truly understand form, which is liable to vanish, as form which is liable to vanish. They truly understand form, which is liable to originate and vanish, as form which is liable to originate and vanish.

22.126.s: Samudayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘samudayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; vayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘vayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ vedanaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammā vedanā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti. Samudayadhammaṁ saññaṁ … samudayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘samudayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; vayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘vayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; samudayavayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘samudayavayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti. Samudayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; vayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘vayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
22.126.e: They truly understand feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, which is liable to originate, as consciousness which is liable to originate. They truly understand consciousness, which is liable to vanish, as consciousness which is liable to vanish. They truly understand consciousness, which is liable to originate and vanish, as consciousness which is liable to originate and vanish.

22.126.s: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu, vijjā; ettāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.126.e: This is called knowledge. And this is how a knowing one is defined.”

22.127.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
22.127.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana. …

22.127.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
“‘avijjā, avijjā’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, avijjā; kittāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti?
22.127.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’. What is ignorance? And how is an ignoramus defined?”

22.127.s: “Idhāvuso assutavā puthujjano samudayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ ‘samudayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti; vayadhammaṁ rūpaṁ …pe… ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
22.127.e: “Reverend, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t truly understand form, which is liable to originate … liable to vanish … liable to originate and vanish, as form which is liable to originate and vanish.

Samudayadhammaṁ saññaṁ …pe… samudayadhamme saṅkhāre …pe… vayadhamme saṅkhāre …pe… samudayavayadhamme saṅkhāre ‘samudayavayadhammā saṅkhārā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti. Samudayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ …pe… samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘samudayavayadhammaṁ viññāṇan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
22.127.e: They don’t truly understand feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, which is liable to originate … liable to vanish … liable to originate and vanish, as consciousness which is liable to originate and vanish.

22.127.s: Ayaṁ vuccati, āvuso, avijjā; ettāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.127.e: This is called ignorance. And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

22.129.s: Bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:

22.129.e: “Reverend, an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t truly understand the gratification, the drawback, and the escape when it comes to form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

22.129.s: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, avijjā; ettāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.129.e: This is called ignorance. And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

22.135.s: Taññeva nidānaṁ. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
22.135.e: The same setting. Sāriputta said to Mahākoṭṭhita:

22.135.s: “‘avijjā, avijjā’ti, āvuso koṭṭhika, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, avijjā; kittāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti?
22.135.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’. What is ignorance? And how is an ignoramus defined?”

22.135.s: “Idhāvuso, assutavā puthujjano rūpaṁ nappajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti. Vedanaṁ nappajānāti …pe… saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti.
22.135.e: “Reverend, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation. They don’t understand feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

22.135.s: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, avijjā; ettāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.135.e: This is called ignorance. And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

22.135.s: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
22.135.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to him:

22.135.s: “‘vijjā, vijjā’ti, āvuso koṭṭhika, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, vijjā; kittāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti?
22.135.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, they speak of this thing called ‘knowledge’. What is knowledge? And how is a knowing one defined?”

22.135.s: “Idhāvuso, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpaṁ pajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti. Vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti.
22.135.e: “Reverend, it’s when a learned noble disciple understands form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation. They understand feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

22.135.s: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, vijjā; ettāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti.
22.135.e: This is called knowledge. And this is how a knowing one is defined.”

22.136.s: “Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, kukkuḷaṁ, vedanā kukkuḷā, saññā kukkuḷā, saṅkhārā kukkuḷā, viññāṇaṁ kukkuḷaṁ.
22.136.e: “Mendicants, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are burning chaff.

22.136.s: Evaṁ passaṁ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
22.136.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

22.136.s: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
22.136.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

22.137.s: “Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo.
22.137.e: “Mendicants, you should give up desire for what is impermanent.

22.137.s: Kiñca, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ? Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo.
22.137.e: And what is impermanent? Form is impermanent; you should give up desire for it.

22.137.s: viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo.
22.137.e: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up desire for it.

22.137.s: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo”ti.
22.137.e: You should give up desire for what is impermanent.”

22.138.s: “Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo rāgo pahātabbo. Kiñca, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ?
22.138.e: “Mendicants, you should give up greed for what is impermanent. And what is impermanent?

22.138.s: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo rāgo pahātabbo.
22.138.e: Form is impermanent; you should give up greed for it.

22.138.s: viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ; tatra vo rāgo pahātabbo.
22.138.e: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up greed for it.

22.138.s: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo rāgo pahātabbo”ti.
22.138.e: You should give up greed for what is impermanent.”

22.139.s: “Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo chandarāgo pahātabbo. Kiñca, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ?
22.139.e: “Mendicants, you should give up desire and greed for what is impermanent. And what is impermanent?

22.139.s: Rūpaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ, tatra vo chandarāgo pahātabbo.
22.139.e: Form is impermanent; you should give up desire and greed for it.

22.139.s: viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ; tatra vo chandarāgo pahātabbo.
22.139.e: Consciousness is impermanent; you should give up desire and greed for it.

22.139.s: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, aniccaṁ; tatra vo chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
22.139.e: You should give up desire and greed for what is impermanent.”

22.140.s: “Yaṁ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo …pe… yaṁ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṁ; tatra vo chando pahātabbo”ti.

22.146.s: “Saddhāpabbajitassa, bhikkhave, kulaputtassa ayamanudhammo hoti— yaṁ rūpe nibbidābahulo vihareyya. Vedanāya …pe… saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe nibbidābahulo vihareyya. Yo rūpe nibbidābahulo viharanto, vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe nibbidābahulo viharanto rūpaṁ parijānāti, vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ parijānāti; so rūpaṁ parijānaṁ vedanaṁ parijānaṁ saññaṁ parijānaṁ saṅkhāre parijānaṁ viññāṇaṁ parijānaṁ parimuccati rūpamhā, parimuccati vedanāya, parimuccati saññāya, parimuccati saṅkhārehi, parimuccati viññāṇamhā, parimuccati jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi; ‘parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.
22.146.e: “Mendicants, when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith, this is what’s in line with the teaching. They should live full of disillusionment for form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. Living in this way, they completely understand form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. Completely understanding form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness, they’re freed from these things. They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re freed from suffering, I say.”

22.147.s: “Saddhāpabbajitassa, bhikkhave, kulaputtassa ayamanudhammo hoti— yaṁ rūpe aniccānupassī vihareyya. Vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe aniccānupassī vihareyya …pe… ‘parimuccati dukkhasmā’ti vadāmī”ti.

22.150.s: “Kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhan”ti?

“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

22.150.s: “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati rūpaṁ upādāya uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ. Vedanāya sati …pe… saññāya sati … saṅkhāresu sati … viññāṇe sati viññāṇaṁ upādāya uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
22.150.e: “When form exists, because of grasping form, pleasure and pain arise in oneself. When feeling … perception … choices … consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness, pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

22.150.s: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
22.150.e: What do you think, mendicants? Is form permanent or impermanent?”

22.150.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

22.150.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would pleasure and pain arise in oneself?”

22.151.e: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does someone regard things like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

22.157.s: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
22.157.e: What do you think, mendicants? Is form permanent or impermanent?”

22.157.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ …pe… api nu taṁ anupādāya uppajjeyyuṁ saṁyojanābhinivesavinibandhā”ti?
22.157.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would fetters, insistence, and shackles arise?”
“Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

22.158.s: “Kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya, kiṁ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṁyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā”ti?
22.158.e: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, do fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise?”
“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

22.158.s: “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṁ upādāya, rūpaṁ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṁyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā. Vedanāya sati … saññāya sati … saṅkhāresu sati … viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṁ upādāya, viññāṇaṁ abhinivissa uppajjanti saṁyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā.
22.158.e: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise. When feeling … perception … choices … consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise.

22.158.s: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
22.158.e: What do you think, mendicants? Is form permanent or impermanent?”

22.158.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ …pe… api nu taṁ anupādāya uppajjeyyuṁ saṁyojanābhinivesavinibandhājjhosānā”ti?
22.158.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would fetters, insistence, shackles, and attachments arise?”
“Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

22.159.s: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe… bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
22.159.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

22.159.s: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
22.159.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

22.159.s: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, ānanda, rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
22.159.e: “What do you think, Ānanda? Is form permanent or impermanent?”

22.159.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
22.159.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

22.159.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
22.159.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

22.159.s: “Vedanā … saññā … saṅkhārā … viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
22.159.e: “Is feeling … perception … choices … consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

22.159.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
22.159.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

22.159.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
22.159.e: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

22.159.s:
Anto dhammakathikā vijjā,
kukkuḷaṁ diṭṭhipañcamaṁ;
Tatiyo paṇṇāsako vutto,
nipātoti pavuccatīti.

23.1.s: Atha kho āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.1.e: Then Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

23.1.s: “‘Māro, māro’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, māro”ti?
23.1.e: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘Māra’. How is Māra defined?”

23.1.s: “Rūpe kho, rādha, sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati. Tasmātiha tvaṁ, rādha, rūpaṁ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa. Ye naṁ evaṁ passanti te sammā passanti. Vedanāya sati … saññāya sati … saṅkhāresu sati … viññāṇe sati māro vā assa māretā vā yo vā pana mīyati. Tasmātiha tvaṁ, rādha, viññāṇaṁ māroti passa, māretāti passa, mīyatīti passa, rogoti passa, gaṇḍoti passa, sallanti passa, aghanti passa, aghabhūtanti passa. Ye naṁ evaṁ passanti, te sammā passantī”ti.
23.1.e: “When there is form, Rādha, there would be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered. So you should see form as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess. Those who see it like this see rightly. When there is feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, there may be Māra, or the murderer, or the murdered. So you should see consciousness as Māra, the murderer, the murdered, the diseased, the boil, the dart, the gloom, the gloominess. Those who see it like this see rightly.”
“But sir, what’s the purpose of seeing rightly?”
“Disillusionment is the purpose of seeing rightly.”
“But sir, what is the purpose of extinguishment?”

23.1.s: “Accayāsi, rādha, pañhaṁ, nāsakkhi pañhassa pariyantaṁ gahetuṁ. Nibbānogadhañhi, rādha, brahmacariyaṁ vussati, nibbānaparāyanaṁ nibbānapariyosānan”ti.
23.1.e: “Your question goes too far, Rādha. You weren’t able to grasp the limit of questioning. For extinguishment is the objective, destination, and culmination of the spiritual life.”

23.2.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.2.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.2.s: “‘satto, satto’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sattoti vuccatī”ti?
23.2.e: “Sir, they speak of this thing called a ‘sentient being’. How is a sentient being defined?”

23.2.s: “Rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati. Vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, tatra satto, tatra visatto, tasmā sattoti vuccati.
23.2.e: “Rādha, when you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form, then a being is spoken of. When you cling, strongly cling, to desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, then a being is spoken of.

23.2.s: Seyyathāpi, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā paṁsvāgārakehi kīḷanti. Yāvakīvañca tesu paṁsvāgārakesu avigatarāgā honti avigatacchandā avigatapemā avigatapipāsā avigatapariḷāhā avigatataṇhā, tāva tāni paṁsvāgārakāni allīyanti keḷāyanti dhanāyanti mamāyanti. Yato ca kho, rādha, kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā tesu paṁsvāgārakesu vigatarāgā honti vigatacchandā vigatapemā vigatapipāsā vigatapariḷāhā vigatataṇhā, atha kho tāni paṁsvāgārakāni hatthehi ca pādehi ca vikiranti vidhamanti viddhaṁsenti vikīḷaniyaṁ karonti.
23.2.e: Suppose some boys or girls were playing with sandcastles. As long as they’re not rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they cling to them, dally with them, treasure them, and treat them as their own. But when they are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for those sandcastles, they scatter, smash, and destroy them with their hands and feet, making them unplayable.

23.2.s: Evameva kho, rādha, tumhepi rūpaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Vedanaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Saññaṁ … saṅkhāre vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Viññāṇaṁ vikiratha vidhamatha viddhaṁsetha vikīḷaniyaṁ karotha taṇhākkhayāya paṭipajjatha. Taṇhākkhayo hi, rādha, nibbānan”ti.
23.2.e: In the same way, you should scatter, smash, and destroy form, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving. You should scatter, smash, and destroy feeling … perception … choices … consciousness, making it unplayable. And you should practice for the ending of craving. For the ending of craving is extinguishment.”

23.3.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.3.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.3.s: “‘bhavanettinirodho, bhavanettinirodho’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, bhavanetti, katamo bhavanettinirodho”ti?
23.3.e: “Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘the cessation of the leash to existence’. What is the leash to existence? And what is the cessation of the leash to existence?”

23.3.s: “Rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā— ayaṁ vuccati bhavanetti. Tesaṁ nirodho bhavanettinirodho.
23.3.e: “Rādha, any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies— this is called the leash to existence. Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.

23.3.s: Vedanāya … saññāya … saṅkhāresu … viññāṇe yo chando …pe… adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā— ayaṁ vuccati bhavanetti. Tesaṁ nirodho bhavanettinirodho”ti.
23.3.e: Any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling … perception … choices … consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies— this is called the leash to existence. Their cessation is the cessation of the leash to existence.”

23.4.s: Āyasmā rādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.4.e: Venerable Rādha went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

23.4.s: “Pariññeyye ca, rādha, dhamme desessāmi pariññañca pariññātāviṁ puggalañca. Taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
23.4.e: “Rādha, I will teach you the things that should be completely understood, complete understanding, and the individual who has completely understood. Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

23.4.s: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā rādho bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca:
23.4.e: “Yes, sir,” Rādha replied. The Buddha said this:

23.4.s: “katame ca, rādha, pariññeyyā dhammā? Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, pariññeyyo dhammo, vedanā pariññeyyo dhammo, saññā pariññeyyo dhammo, saṅkhārā pariññeyyo dhammo, viññāṇaṁ pariññeyyo dhammo. Ime vuccanti, rādha, pariññeyyā dhammā.
23.4.e: “And what things should be completely understood? Form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. These are called the things that should be completely understood.

23.4.s: Katamā ca, rādha, pariññā? Yo kho, rādha, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo— ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, pariññā.
23.4.e: And what is complete understanding? The ending of greed, hate, and delusion. This is called complete understanding.

23.4.s: Katamo ca, rādha, pariññātāvī puggalo? ‘Arahā’tissa vacanīyaṁ. Yvāyaṁ āyasmā evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto— ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, pariññātāvī puggalo”ti.
23.4.e: And what is the individual who has completely understood? It should be said: a perfected one, the venerable of such name and such clan. This is called the individual who has completely understood.”

23.5.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.5.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.5.s: “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
23.5.e: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates. What five? The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

23.5.s: Ye hi keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti; na me te, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca pana te āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṁ vā brahmaññatthaṁ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
23.5.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape. I don’t deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and don’t live having realized it with their own insight in this very life.

23.5.s: Ye ca kho keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti; te kho me, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti.
23.5.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ gratification, drawback, and escape. I deem them as true ascetics and brahmins. Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

23.6.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.6.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.6.s: “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
23.6.e: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates. What five? The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

23.6.s: Ye hi keci, rādha, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
23.6.e: There are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape … Those venerables don’t realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin …
There are ascetics and brahmins who do truly understand … Those venerables realize the goal of life as an ascetic or brahmin, and live having realized it with their own insight.”

23.7.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.7.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.7.s: “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Yato kho, rādha, ariyasāvako imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti— ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti.
23.7.e: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates. What five? The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. When a noble disciple truly understands these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape, they’re called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

23.8.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.8.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.8.s: “pañcime, rādha, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Yato kho, rādha, bhikkhu imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upādānakkhandhānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti— ayaṁ vuccati, rādha, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṁyojano sammadaññāvimutto”ti.
23.8.e: “Rādha, there are these five grasping aggregates. What five? The grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. A mendicant comes to be freed by not grasping after truly understanding these five grasping aggregates’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape. Such a mendicant is called a perfected one, with defilements ended, who has completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and is rightly freed through enlightenment.”

23.9.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.9.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.9.s: “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha. Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
23.9.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form. Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

23.9.s: Vedanāya yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha. Evaṁ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā. Saññāya … saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha. Evaṁ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā. Viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā, taṁ pajahatha. Evaṁ taṁ viññāṇaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati …pe… anuppādadhamman”ti.
23.9.e: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling … perception … choices … consciousness. Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

23.10.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.10.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.10.s: “rūpe kho, rādha, yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṁ taṁ rūpaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhammaṁ.
23.10.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for form; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. Thus that form will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

23.10.s: Vedanāya yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṁ sā vedanā pahīnā bhavissati ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā. Saññāya … saṅkhāresu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṁ te saṅkhārā pahīnā bhavissanti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā. Viññāṇe yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye upayupādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahatha. Evaṁ taṁ viññāṇaṁ pahīnaṁ bhavissati ucchinnamūlaṁ tālāvatthukataṁ anabhāvaṅkataṁ āyatiṁ anuppādadhamman”ti.
23.10.e: You should give up any desire, greed, relishing, and craving for feeling … perception … choices … consciousness; and any attraction, grasping, mental fixation, insistence, and underlying tendencies. Thus that consciousness will be given up, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.”

23.11.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.11.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.11.s: “‘māro, māro’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, māro”ti?
23.11.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘Māra’. How is Māra defined?”

23.11.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māro, vedanā māro, saññā māro, saṅkhārā māro, viññāṇaṁ māro.
23.11.e: “Rādha, form is Māra, feeling is Māra, perception is Māra, choices are Māra, consciousness is Māra.

23.11.s: Evaṁ passaṁ, rādha, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṁ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṁ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṁ hoti.
23.11.e: Seeing this, a learned noble disciple grows disillusioned with form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness. Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away they’re freed. When they’re freed, they know they’re freed.

23.11.s: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.
23.11.e: They understand: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.12.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.12.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.12.s: “‘māradhammo, māradhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, māradhammo”ti?
23.12.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘Māra nature’. What is of Māra nature?”

23.12.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māradhammo, vedanā māradhammo, saññā māradhammo, saṅkhārā māradhammo, viññāṇaṁ māradhammo.
23.12.e: “Rādha, form is of Māra nature. Feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of Māra nature.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.13.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.13.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.13.s: “‘aniccaṁ, aniccan’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṁ nu kho, bhante, aniccan”ti?
23.13.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘impermanence’. What has impermanent nature?”

23.13.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, aniccaṁ, vedanā aniccā, saññā aniccā, saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṁ aniccaṁ.
23.13.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are impermanent.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.14.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.14.s: “‘aniccadhammo, aniccadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, aniccadhammo”ti?
23.14.e: “Sir, they speak of having ‘impermanent nature’. What is of impermanent nature?”

23.14.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, aniccadhammo, vedanā aniccadhammo, saññā aniccadhammo, saṅkhārā aniccadhammo, viññāṇaṁ aniccadhammo.
23.14.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of impermanent nature.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.15.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.15.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.15.s: “‘dukkhaṁ, dukkhan’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṁ nu kho, bhante, dukkhan”ti?
23.15.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘suffering’. What is suffering?”

23.15.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhaṁ, vedanā dukkhā, saññā dukkhā, saṅkhārā dukkhā, viññāṇaṁ dukkhaṁ.
23.15.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are suffering.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.16.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.16.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.16.s: “‘dukkhadhammo, dukkhadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, dukkhadhammo”ti?
23.16.e: “Sir, they speak of having ‘suffering nature’. What is of a nature to suffer?”

23.16.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, dukkhadhammo, vedanā dukkhadhammo, saññā dukkhadhammo, saṅkhārā dukkhadhammo, viññāṇaṁ dukkhadhammo.
23.16.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are of a nature to suffer.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.17.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.17.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.17.s: “‘anattā, anattā’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, anattā”ti?
23.17.e: “Sir, they speak of ‘not-self’. What is not-self?”

23.17.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṁ anattā.
23.17.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness are not-self.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.18.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.18.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.18.s: “‘anattadhammo, anattadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, anattadhammo”ti?
23.18.e: “Sir, they speak of having ‘not-self nature’. What has a nature of not-self?”

23.18.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, anattadhammo, vedanā anattadhammo, saññā anattadhammo, saṅkhārā anattadhammo, viññāṇaṁ anattadhammo.
23.18.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a nature of not-self.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.19.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.19.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.19.s: “‘khayadhammo, khayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, khayadhammo”ti?
23.19.e: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to end’. What has a liability to end?”

23.19.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, khayadhammo, vedanā khayadhammo, saññā khayadhammo, saṅkhārā khayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ khayadhammo.
23.19.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to end.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.20.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.20.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.20.s: “‘vayadhammo, vayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, vayadhammo”ti?
23.20.e: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to fall’. What has a liability to fall?”

23.20.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, vayadhammo, vedanā vayadhammo, saññā vayadhammo, saṅkhārā vayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ vayadhammo.
23.20.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to fall.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.21.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.21.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.21.s: “‘samudayadhammo, samudayadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, samudayadhammo”ti?
23.21.e: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to originate’. What has a liability to originate?”

23.21.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, samudayadhammo, vedanā samudayadhammo, saññā samudayadhammo, saṅkhārā samudayadhammo, viññāṇaṁ samudayadhammo.
23.21.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to originate.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.22.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.22.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.22.s: “‘nirodhadhammo, nirodhadhammo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, bhante, nirodhadhammo”ti?
23.22.e: “Sir, they speak of a ‘liability to cease’. What has a liability to cease?”

23.22.s: “Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo, vedanā nirodhadhammo, saññā nirodhadhammo, saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo, viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo.
23.22.e: “Rādha, form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness have a liability to cease.
Seeing this … They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

23.23-33.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
23.23-33.e: Seated to one side, Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.23-33.s: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
23.23-33.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

23.23-33.s: “Yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, māro? Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
23.23-33.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra. And what is Māra? Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

23.23-33.s: Vedanā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saññā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saṅkhārā māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
viññāṇaṁ māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe… yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
23.23-33.e: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

23.23-33.s: “Yo kho, rādha, māradhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….
23.23-33.e: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of Māra nature …”

23.23-33.s: “Yo kho, rādha, samudayadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….

23.34.e: Venerable Rādha said to the Buddha:

23.34.s: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
23.34.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

23.34.s: “Yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, nirodhadhammo? Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
23.34.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease. And what is of a nature to cease? Form is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

23.34.s: vedanā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saññā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
saṅkhārā nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe… yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
23.34.e: Consciousness is of a nature to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is of a nature to cease.”

23.35-45.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.35-45.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.35-45.s: “yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, māro? Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe…
23.35-45.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra. And what is Māra? Form is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. …

23.35-45.s: viññāṇaṁ māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo …pe… yo kho, rādha, māro; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
23.35-45.e: Consciousness is Māra. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is Māra.”

23.35-45.s: “Yo kho, rādha, māradhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….
23.35-45.e: “You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is subject to Māra …”

23.35-45.s: “Yo kho, rādha, samudayadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo …pe….

23.46.s: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rādhaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
23.46.e: When Venerable Rādha was seated to one side, the Buddha said to him:

23.46.s: “yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, nirodhadhammo? Rūpaṁ kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo.
23.46.e: “Rādha, you should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease. And what is liable to cease? Form is liable to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it.

23.46.s: viññāṇaṁ nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo. Yo kho, rādha, nirodhadhammo; tatra te chando pahātabbo, rāgo pahātabbo, chandarāgo pahātabbo”ti.
23.46.e: Consciousness is liable to cease. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for it. You should give up any desire, any greed, any desire and greed for whatever is liable to cease.”

24.1.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane. Bhagavā etadavoca:
24.1.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove. The Buddha said this:

24.1.s: “kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya, kiṁ abhinivissa evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjati: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti?
24.1.e: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

24.1.s: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaññeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
24.1.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

24.1.s: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
24.1.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

24.1.s: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ. Bhagavā etadavoca:
24.1.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this:

24.1.s: “Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṁ upādāya, rūpaṁ abhinivissa evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjati: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti. Vedanāya sati …pe… saññāya sati … saṅkhāresu sati … viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṁ upādāya, viññāṇaṁ abhinivissa evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjati: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’ti.
24.1.e: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar.’ When feeling … perception … choices … consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness, the view arises: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar.’

24.1.s: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: What do you think, mendicants? Is form permanent or impermanent?”

24.1.s: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Impermanent, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

24.1.s: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Suffering, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti?
24.1.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

24.1.s: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “No, sir.”

24.1.s: “Vedanā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti … “saññā … saṅkhārā … viññāṇaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: “Is feeling … perception … choices … consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

24.1.s: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Impermanent, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

24.1.s: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Suffering, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti?
24.1.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

24.1.s: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “No, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yampidaṁ diṭṭhaṁ sutaṁ mutaṁ viññātaṁ pattaṁ pariyesitaṁ anuvicaritaṁ manasā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: “That which is seen, heard, thought, known, attained, sought, and explored by the mind: is that permanent or impermanent?”

24.1.s: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Impermanent, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
24.1.e: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

24.1.s: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “Suffering, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya: ‘na vātā vāyanti, na najjo sandanti, na gabbhiniyo vijāyanti, na candimasūriyā udenti vā apenti vā esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā’”ti?
24.1.e: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise: ‘Winds don’t blow; rivers don’t flow; pregnant women don’t give birth; the moon and stars neither rise nor set, but stand firm like a pillar’?”

24.1.s: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
24.1.e: “No, sir.”

24.1.s: “Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhasamudayepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti— ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti.
24.1.e: “When a noble disciple has given up doubt regarding these six grounds, and has given up doubt in suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation, they’re called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
